newsitem.title: USA: Gateway 2000 says laptop sales boost earnings.
newsitem.headline: Gateway 2000 says laptop sales boost earnings.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc. said Thursday that earnings rose 10 percent in the second quarter, boosted by record sales of its Gateway Solo laptop computers and strong revenue growth overseas.
Second quarter net income hit $56.5 million, up from $51.4 million in the same year-ago period. Revenues rose 23 percent to $1.39 billion from $1.14 billion.
Earnings per share were 36 cents after adjusting for a two-for-one stock split, matching analysts' forecasts and up from 33 cents a share a year ago.
Gateway said it shipped 554,000 personal computers during the quarter, a 31 percent increase from year-earlier shipments of 424,000 units.
The company, based in North Sioux City, S.D., said shipments of laptop machines more than doubled from the year-ago quarter.
But its average unit price fell 6 percent in the quarter to $2,515, resulting in smaller growth in sales than in shipments.
In Europe, shipments jumped 47 percent for the period, while shipments in the Asia-Pacific region climbed 90 percent.
Gateway, which bypasses retailers and sells directly to customers, said weaker-than-expected demand early in the quarter caused a build-up in inventory.
"Demand did not accelerate as fast as we thought until the end of the quarter, resulting in higher than desired inventory levels," Chairman Ted Waitt said in a statement.
Industry analysts said they were concerned about the inventory growth, because direct marketers rely on a "build-to-order" models to avoid financing inventory.
But analysts said the company probably will cut inventory levels in the second half of the year through price cuts.
"I wasn't expecting them to end the quarter with a lot of inventory that they have to move," said Daniel Ries at Nomura Securities.
Gateway stock fell $1.56 to $43.19 on the New York Stock Exchange. It reported results after the close of trading.
